evidence.multi_round_behaviour: while _calls: stop on no further declared calls, rounds_this_turn >= fetch_rounds_per_turn(cfg), or fetch_rounds_used >= fetch_rounds_per_arm(cfg). Each follow-up is re-parsed with arm_cd.parse_fetch_calls_from_response(resp, tool_names=fetch_call_tool_names(cfg)). _flush_d_rows() runs at the top of each round after both guards pass, so every paid request's row is on disk before the next send and the last follow-up's row is still left to the turn row (rows == sends).
evidence.ref_availability: NO. The ARM_D prompt never lists the available refs. Planner.build (run_longrun.py:1732) starts from working_set_block (run_longrun.py:1747); its INDEX lines come from index_lines (run_longrun.py:366-373) and read '- @knowledge:{item[id]}@1 {hash8} {len}' -- item ids in the @knowledge: namespace, not doc-<name>@r<rev> refs. Real refs reach the model only as [MASKED <ref>] markers on masked turns (run_longrun.py:1760, make_ref = {doc_id}@r{revision}) or as TOOL_OUTPUT (doc_id@rev) lines on the delivery turn. checkpoint_prompt (run_longrun.py:2366-2385) teaches the ref FORM plus three example refs (doc-config@r1, doc-constants@r1, doc-errors@r1) that need not exist. The 12 bad refs are consistent with guessing from the INDEX: knowledge/item-1@1 and knowledge/item-1 are the INDEX id form; ptr_engine/resolve.py and knowledge/doc-fact-02.txt are path-shaped guesses.
